articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Threat Detection: A Study on Malicious URL Classification
abstract: In today’s digital age, the internet serves as a vital resource. However, it poses significant risks from malicious websites that threaten cybersecurity. This study focuses on developing effective threat detection methods to identify harmful URLs using machine learning models, specifically Random Forest and XGBoost, to classify URL types such as benign, phishing, malware, and defacement. A comprehensive feature extraction process trains the classification models for real-time analysis of URL threats. The findings indicate that the Random Forest model outperforms XGBoost, particularly in classifying phishing URLs, while demonstrating robust accuracy despite challenges with overfitting. This research culminates in the creation of an Android-based Malicious URL Detector mobile application that integrates the trained model, aiming to enhance cybersecurity defenses. By leveraging machine learning techniques, this study contributes to more efficient and effective detection of malicious URLs, fostering a safer online environment for users.

articleTitle: A Self-Adaptive Waste Management System Employing Convolutional Neural Network for Real-Time Categorization
abstract: The exponential and dramatic rise in urbanization and industrialization has made waste management a critical global issue. As the global population reaches unprecedented levels, so has the production of waste reached degrees where it has become uncontrollable. In this study, we present a self-adaptive waste management system leveraging the power of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for real-time categorization of waste. The proposed system employs a robust CNN model trained on a diverse dataset of waste images, enabling it to accurately identify and segregate various types of waste, including plastics, metals, organic materials, and paper. By utilizing real-time image processing and adaptive learning capabilities, the system continually improves its classification accuracy, adapting to new waste types and environmental conditions. The system was tested using Yolov8 module configured with a specially tailored dataset designed to exclusively detect and classify metallic, plastic, and paper waste. The custom-trained model demonstrated high accuracy in identifying metallic and paper waste, achieving 220 and 140 true positives during the validation phase. However, the model struggled to reliably detect plastics, registering only 56 true positives. This suggests that object detection algorithms may encounter challenges when identifying objects with clear and transparent properties, as seen with plastics and polymers. This difficulty is further evidenced by the false positive score of 60, indicating that the model frequently misidentified plastics as background. Overall, the model implemented in the proposed system achieved precision scores of $90.7 \%, 69.1 \%$ and $82.8 \%$ for metals, plastics, and paper, respectively.

articleTitle: Data Breach Notifications and Their Completeness
abstract: Data quality in documentation is crucial for organizations to access and analyze data. It plays a vital role when we analyze security breach documents and data breach notifications. The critical data quality dimensions are completeness, uniqueness, timeliness, validity, accuracy, and consistency. This paper analyzes the completeness of 10 Washington state data breach notification documents to explain how completeness plays a critical role in breach notifications to understand data breaches. If the data breach notifications are incomplete, this hinder analysis and have a larger potential to mislead the analysis and different results due to the missing information. This analysis compares the 10 data breach notifications with the Washington State data breach notification form to test their completeness and provide the findings.

articleTitle: Detecting Digital Audio Drugs Using Deep learning
abstract: Digital drugs, auditory illusions created by playing slightly different frequencies in each ear, can influence mental states. Experiments were conducted using MATLAB 2023b on hardware with specifications of processor intel core i7 and graphic card NVIDIA GeForce GTX 4070. A dataset has a total of 7,000 audio files, divided into 5,000 audio drug files embedded with binaural beats and 1,000 original audio files from various categories. This database used to train and evaluate deep learning model to detect and classify audio drugs. Inception MV4 model was trained using SGDM optimizer over 3 epochs with different values of learning rates, achieving high performance metrics and demonstrating its efficacy in classification tasks. Inception MV4 model achieved average accuracies 99.9733% with learning rates 1e-3 and 1e-4, and an average accuracy 98.8833% with a learning rate 1e-5.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of LIME and SHAP for Enhancing Trustworthiness and Efficiency in Explainable AI Systems
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a solution in almost every domain, significantly improving our lives. AI’s ability to efficiently extract important features and find valuable patterns from large amounts of data enables faster task completion. However, concerns have been raised about the opacity of decision-making processes in ‘black box’ AI models. This has led to the development of explainable AI (XAI), which aims to make AI systems more transparent and understandable to users. Several XAI methods have been developed with different approaches and outputs. This paper aims to compare the state-of-the-art explainability approaches, with a particular analysis of methods based on feature importance, such as the well-known Local Interpretable Modelagnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) methods. Experiments are conducted with several machine learning methods on two datasets. This paper presents a comparison of LIME and SHAP, which can be used as a reference in selecting an XAI method according to data characteristics and explanation goals. LIME excels in performing local explanations through interpretable models, making it relatively easy to implement. However, LIME explanations are not very stable across tests due to instance perturbations. In contrast, SHAP provides consistent explanations based on Shapley game theory by computing Shapley values that ensure fair feature contributions across the dataset. Despite its computational overhead, SHAP offers more robust and global insights compared to LIME.

articleTitle: Exploring TikTok as an Educational Tool: Student Insights and Perspectives
abstract: The rise of social media has significantly influenced various aspects of daily life, including education. Among these platforms, TikTok stands out for its engaging short videos that captivate millions globally. Initially perceived as purely for entertainment, TikTok has piqued interest as a potential educational tool. This study explores TikTok’s educational viability by assessing student experiences and perceptions. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach, the study surveyed 50 students from the National University Dasmariñas, combining quantitative data on TikTok usage patterns with qualitative insights into its educational effectiveness. The survey revealed that $\mathbf{7 0 \%}$ of respondents frequently used TikTok, with $\mathbf{6 0 \%}$ employing the platform for learning. Preferred subject areas included Science and Math, aligning with Mayer’s Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, which emphasizes the benefits of combining auditory and visual information. Qualitative data provided more profound insights into student motivations, highlighting TikTok’s accessibility and engaging format as critical factors. Students appreciated the platform’s ability to present complex topics in bite-sized, digestible chunks. However, concerns about the short format limiting in-depth exploration and the need for accuracy were noted. The study concludes that while TikTok holds promise as a supplementary educational tool, especially for initial knowledge acquisition and visual learning, it should be integrated thoughtfully with traditional methods to address its limitations. Future research should explore strategies for effectively leveraging TikTok in formal education, ensuring quality control, and enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition: The Role of Hybrid Feature Extraction Technique in Accelerometer Data Using a Voting Classifier Approach
abstract: Human Activity Recognition has become an increasingly important research area with applications in various domains, including healthcare, sports, and smart home technologies. This study presents a comprehensive approach to human activity recognition using a combination of time-domain and frequency-domain feature extraction with advanced feature extraction techniques along with a voting classifier model. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a comprehensive evaluation was conducted using publicly available datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed voting-based ensemble method with hybrid feature extraction significantly improved the accuracy of human activity recognition compared to individual classifiers and other ensemble models.

articleTitle: Exploring Opportunity of Large Language Model for Job Vacancy Extractions
abstract: In recent years, the growth of Online Job Vacancies (OJVs) has provided a valuable opportunity for researchers and practitioners to gain insights into the Job Market. However, this opportunity has not been effectively utilized in Indonesia, leading to issues such as the mismatch between curriculum and industry needs. This research aims to explore the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract information from Online Job Vacancies, focusing on key variables such as skills and tools. By developing a tailored Prompt Chain, this research successfully extracted relevant information from 312 OJVs. The evaluation was conducted using semantic precision and recall metrics, achieving precision scores of 97.783% for skills and 99.140% for tools, and recall scores of 90.167% for skills and 95.071% for tools. This evaluation was validated by a LinkedIn Top Voice 2024, who assessed the semantic similarity between the extracted outputs and the established ground truth. This expert-guided evaluation highlights the potential of LLMs in Labor Market Intelligent tools and job matching systems. The findings contribute to understanding the strengths and limitations of LLMs in semantic text extraction, offering insights into their future scalability and adaptation across various job sectors.

articleTitle: Masked Theme-Specific Named Entity Recognition Assisted with Large Language Models
abstract: Existing Named Entity Recognition (NER) methods are required to label relevant samples and train the concrete NER models. Due to the specification of theme-specific documents, these NER models are considerably hard to identify potential theme-specific entities. To address this challenge, we propose an effective two-stage approach of masked theme-specific NER associated with Large Language Models (LLMs), which uses the unsupervised mechanism rather than the supervised one. The approach involves theme-specific entity ontology construction and masked NER in heterogeneous documents. The first stage is associated with LLMs and Wikipedia category pages, and the second one is implemented with the masked NER based on the created ontology in the first stage. Extensive experimental results suggest that the proposed masked NER can precisely locate the known entities in the theme-specific entity ontology while improving the accuracy of NER in the remaining text. Compared to the mainstream NER frameworks such as spaCy 3, the masked NER can identify more valid entities in the input Markdown text and continuously use the newly detected unknown entities to update the created ontology.

articleTitle: Addressing Distortion in Social Distance Monitoring: Calibration for Accurate Distance Calculation
abstract: The Social Distance Monitoring (SDM) system is a technology-driven solution that aims to enforce and maintain social distancing rules. During epidemics such as COVID-19, practising physical distancing is crucial to prevent the transmission of infectious diseases. This study focuses on the utilisation of the OpenPose algorithm for human detection, which effectively detects humans and identifies key points such as eyes-to-feet points as human height. These points enable the calculation of the distance between individuals and the width of each person. To ensure accurate distance measurement, a perspective transformation is applied to each frame after human detection, effectively addressing distortion issues caused by variations in camera angles. A novel calibration process is also introduced to handle situations where the video’s viewing angle exceeds a certain threshold, resulting in distortion. The calibration process calculates the distance ratio using frame partitioning, improving the precision of distance measurement. This study contributes to the advancement of social distance monitoring systems, providing an effective calibration solution for enforcing social distancing rules.

articleTitle: Methods of Generating the Context Graph and Its Summarization for Understanding the Elaboration Circumstances of Research Documents
abstract: In the elaboration work of research documents, which is an essential component of proceeding with research activities, it is important to sufficiently understand the elaboration contexts (e.g., the deliverables and the work history) so that they can be used in later work. However, the number of documents involved can become enormous, and work histories are inevitably complicated when research activities continue for a long period of time. Therefore, it becomes increasingly difficult to grasp the elaboration contexts. In our research, we aim to support the understanding of work circumstances by generating an elaboration context graph that organizes the contexts of elaboration work of research documents. In this paper, we mainly describe a method for graph summarization to enable easy understanding of the elaboration context graph, which can become quite large with long-term research activities. We also describe a case study in which we generated and summarized an elaboration context graph using actual history data, and discuss the effectiveness of the proposed methods on the basis of the results.

articleTitle: Visualization of Matching Status Between Emphasis by a Presenter and Attention by Audiences for Supporting Refinement of Presentation Slides
abstract: To present a clear and effective presentation, it is crucial to carefully refine presentation slides and the portions which a presenter emphasizes on the slides. There is also a significant impact on the audience’s comprehension due to factors such as the amount of text, presence of figures and tables, and their layout on the slide. Although slide refinement should consider audience reactions during presentation rehearsals, it is often difficult for a presenter to sufficiently grasp such reactions. This research aims to develop a system for supporting presentation-slide refinement by taking into account the matching status between the emphasis of a presenter and attention of the audience. For this paper, we propose methods for extracting the emphasis of a presenter on the basis of the analysis of the structural features of slides and extracting the attention of the audience on the basis of gaze analysis. We also describe the visualization of their matching status along with snapshots of a prototype of our support system and the accuracy and characteristics of the proposed methods on the basis of the results of experiments on extracting the emphasis of a presenter and attention of the audience using our prototype.

Author Keywords: visualization of matching status between emphasis and attention

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition: Music Generation using Convolutional Neural Network Approach
abstract: Music has long been an inseparable companion to humanity, enriching our lives and experiences. Life would feel dull without music, as it plays a vital role in expressing emotions. Considering that music has a powerful effect on human emotions, people frequently use it as a form of therapy to manage and control their anxiety. There is limited study on the recognition of emotional speech among people and the subsequent generation of music based on their present emotional state. Further investigation is required to explore methods for generating music that aligns with the user’s present emotional state. This research applies the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze the Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) spectrogram. The MFCC spectrogram is derived from the speech emotion recognition (SER) signal and utilized to generate music by identifying emotional states. A sad or happy emotion is produced by generating music that can improve the person’s mood based on the mood captured. The experiment shows that the CNN classifier model successfully achieved an accuracy of 80.61% during the training phase. Aside from that, utilizing Adam and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimizers, the study compares their efficacy in enhancing model accuracy and reliability. The findings reveal that specific configurations of dropout rates and epochs, combined with the choice of optimizer, significantly impact the model’s effectiveness in emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Wearable Pain Detector Using Heart Rate and Skin Conductance
abstract: Pain not only impacts the physical condition but is also influenced by physiological factors that play a role in amplifying or influencing pain. A common approach used to manage pain is the use of opioids. The use of opioids in pain management has risks, especially overdose due to inappropriate use. One factor that can contribute to overdose is the lack of objective pain assessment. One method to assess pain is the visual analog scale. Due to its subjective nature, this can lead to inconsistent and inaccurate assessments. To overcome this impact, a wearable pain detector was developed that is designed to detect pain by combining two physiological parameters, namely heart rate activity and skin conductance, which produces a pain scale with a range of 0-10, and provides classification with categories ranging from “no pain” to “most severe pain”. The classification process is performed using the simple linear regression method. Overall, the wearable pain detector had an accuracy of 75% in calculating the pain scale of the subject. The product is designed in the form of a wearable device that resembles a watch, making it comfortable for patients to use.

articleTitle: Designing a Cost-Effective IoT Air Quality Sensor for Real-Time Data Monitoring
abstract: This research presents the design and implementation of a cost-effective, IoT-based air quality monitoring system for real-time environmental assessment. The system integrates ZH03A and MQ-7 sensors to measure particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) and carbon monoxide (CO) levels, respectively, managed by an Arduino Uno microcontroller for data processing. The system displays measurements on a $20 \times 4$ LCD and transmits real-time data via a NodeMCU ESP8266 to the Thinger.io cloud platform. In addition, data is stored locally on a microSD card and visualized as air quality maps using GIS tools. The system’s performance was validated through comparative testing with BMKG’s operational instruments, including the Kimoto ACSA-14 and LGR CO-30r. Field testing across 50 locations in South Jakarta revealed average concentrations of PM2.5 ($60 \mu \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$), PM10 ($70 \mu \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$), and CO (6.55 ppm), classified as “unhealthy,” “moderate,” and “moderate” under the AQI. This system provides an affordable and scalable solution for monitoring urban air quality, offering stakeholders real-time insights and actionable data. It aims to enhance public awareness and support data-driven policy interventions for improved environmental management

articleTitle: The Influence of Digital Leadership, Digital Capabilities, and Organizational Innovation on Organizational Sustainability in the automotive industry
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of digital leadership, digital capability, and organizational innovation on organizational sustainability in the automobile industry. This study used a survey methodology, with main data from 263 dealership and workshop workers working in various automotive companies in Greater Jakarta. This study’s independent variables include Digital Leadership, Digital Capability, and Organizational Innovation, with Organizational Sustainability as the dependent variable. To determine how the independent variables affect the dependent variable, the acquired data will be analyzed using quantitative research methods. The study’s findings are likely to expand awareness of the role of digital leadership, digital capability, and organizational innovation in increasing organizational sustainability in the automobile industry.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wireless Network Performance with Decision Tree-Based Gain Prediction
abstract: This study investigates the optimization of wireless network performance using decision tree-based gain prediction. A simulation involving 100 users, uniformly distributed around a central Access Point (AP), calculates the Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) for each user, based on their distance and angle relative to the AP. The resulting dataset captures relationships between user positions and network performance metrics. A Decision Tree Regressor predicts continuous gain values, while a Decision Tree Classifier categorizes gains into discrete classes. The regression model demonstrates high accuracy with strong correlation, and the classification model achieves notable accuracy and recall, validated through confusion matrices and classification reports. Simulations evaluate the impact of both normal and predicted gains on network throughput and delay, showing that predicted gains closely approximate outcomes seen with normal gain calculations. These findings highlight the potential of decision tree models for optimizing network configurations and fine-tuning parameters to improve overall network performance.

articleTitle: Exploring TikTok Content in Indonesia: Education, News, and Personal Experience in the Crypto Niche
abstract: TikTok has emerged as a dominant platform for sharing information and education, especially in Indonesia’s rapidly growing crypto sector. This study investigates how TikTok shapes understanding of cryptocurrency in Indonesia, with a focus on the unique role of TikTok influencers in spreading knowledge about digital financial revolution. By analyzing the type of content being shared and its impact on public knowledge, This research aims to uncover trends in using TikTok as a crypto education and awareness tool in Indonesia. This research uses a cross-sectional study by analyzing popular hashtags related to cryptocurrency content since 2024. A deductive qualitative analysis was used to identify relevant accounts and content. As the result, crypto content on TikTok is dominated by crypto trend topics, with educational formats being the most dominant, with the majority of creators identifying themselves as traders and consistently showing their faces in videos. The research is limited by its focus on TikTok and sample size and focus on one social media platform.

articleTitle: Methods of Forming Learner Groups for Mutual Teaching among Leaners with Different Situations in Programming Exercise
abstract: In response to the growing demand for developing programming skills, opportunities for providing programming exercises have been increasing at educational institutions such as universities. Instructors must be attentive to learners’ progress and situations to provide effective support. However, there are limits to supporting a large number of learners by a small number of instructors. Peer or group-based learning has been recognized as a promising approach to address these challenges, but most existing methods rely on static group formation based on pre-exercise information. We developed methods for forming dynamic learning groups that leverage learners’ current situations for effective peer-assisted learning. This paper mainly describes the dynamic formation of learner groups taking into account multiple factors such as whether learners are struggling and the similarity between source codes. We also describe the experiments on forming learner groups and discuss the basic effectiveness of the proposed methods on the basis of the experimental results.

articleTitle: Study on Potential Interferences of 5G NR-U and WiFi 6E to Fixed Service in 6 GHz
abstract: This paper studies coexistence scenarios and observed potential interferences from services using unlicensed bands, Radio Local Area Network (RLAN) and 5G New Radio unlicensed (5G NR-U), to services using licensed band, Fixed service (FS). These interferences have the potential to disrupt FS if it exceeds established thresholds for protection criteria. To assess the impact of this coexistence, we develop several scenarios that focus on FS as the primary receiver to be protected and analyze potential interferences from RLAN and 5G NR-U. We perform a series of computer simulations for scenarios with varying power levels, series of distances, and number of devices under multipath fading channels. FS parameters are set using the practical parameters of the real-field in suburban Indonesia. We evaluate Interference-to-noise power ratio (INR) and Signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) at the FS receiver. Our results show that coexistence is feasible without causing interference to FS, when minimum separation distances and maximum number of devices for each station are well managed.

articleTitle: Sustainable Farming Gamification for Vocational High School Students in Indonesia
abstract: The decline in farmer population and sustainable agriculture are two issues to be solved for Indonesia to sustain its large population. The former are caused by many factors such as rapid urbanization and the conversion of farmland into housing areas or industrial zones. The latter concerns about sustainable farming practices in line with the Sustainable Development Goal envisioned by the United Nations. An approach to solve these two problems is to educate many young Indonesians in the agricultural occupation, especially those who enroll in vocational high school. The vocational high school students become the focus because when they graduate and partake in farming occupation, they will regenerate the aging farming population. This approach should also ensure a focus on sustainable agriculture practices such as using organic fertilizer. Furthermore, because the young population in Indonesia falls under generation Z or younger, this requires a modern approach to deliver the lesson, especially via gamification. To support this effort, this research proposes a gamification to teach sustainable agriculture to first-year students enrolled in vocational high school. Results from evaluation study shows that 7 of 8 teachers agreed that the gamification represents learning material they used to teach in the classroom.

articleTitle: Developing And Executing Pedagogical Virtual Game-Based Learning for Java Programming
abstract: The integration of game-based learning into computer science education has shown considerable promise in improving student engagement and academic achievement, particularly in Java programming. This paper examines the creation and execution of a pedagogical virtual game-based learning environment for adult learners in higher education, with a focus on Java programming. The environment enhances students’ programming abilities by incorporating fundamental educational concepts, such as intrinsic motivation, active learning, and constructivism, via interactive projects and gamification elements, including drag-and-drop exercises, challenges, and immediate feedback. The study highlights design considerations, including game design elements like challenge, curiosity, and control, which are essential for creating an engaging learning experience. The testing of the system, involving 30 students, demonstrated significant improvements in both engagement and comprehension of Java programming concepts. This research demonstrates that game-based learning environments possess considerable potential to alleviate issues in programming education, such as high dropout rates and varying skill levels, by offering an engaging and adaptive platform tailored for adult learners.

articleTitle: CamouFlair - Hybrid Steganography for Short Secure Messaging
abstract: Nowadays, it is difficult to send information secretly on the Internet. Normally, the data involved in that communication will go through a long path before arriving at the desired destination. Because of that, there is a high possibility of someone monitoring the communication, trying to gain benefit out of the information being passed around. Although, there are already many security systems being developed, even now, it is just a matter of time before they are exposed. Therefore, this study proposes a new steganography method to supplement the effort of providing secure messaging. The proposed method will be based on a hybrid steganography method consisting of image and text steganography. Before being embedded, the message will be encrypted using symmetric key encryption namely AES. Next, the encrypted message will be embedded into a list of verse names of Quran. Sequentially, the result from that process will then be embedded into a cover image through custom implementation of Discrete Cosine Transformation (DCT) which will produce a stegofile, ready to be transported to the receiver. Through the testing done, it can be concluded that the implementation done in this study is comparable to those of the existing implementation of DCT for short message.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of a PWM-Based Digital Communication System for High-Speed Data Transfer
abstract: The goal of this project is to design and implement a communication system using Pulse Width Modulation (Abbreviated in the text as PWM) technology. The system uses binary data to represent ASCII characters. It transmits and receives data through the PWM_Sender and PWM_Receiver modules. The communication signal is encoded in PWM form, with a minimum data transmission rate of 9600 baud. The implementation carried out on the DE10 Standard development board. Key objectives include developing a transmitter module that converts input binary data into PWM signal periods and widths, a PWM generation module that creates and sends PWM signals based on the provided period and width parameters, and a receiver module that decodes these PWM signals back into their original binary data. This project demonstrates the practical application of PWM in digital communication systems, with a focus on its implementation on the FPGA DE10 Standard development board.

articleTitle: Integrating Serious Game in Personalized Learning Environment
abstract: Computer science skills have become very important in the careers of STEM fields in today’s digital economy. However, many students often struggle in grasping programming concepts, leading to high dropout rates in computer science courses. The students have also found traditional learning environment to be ineffective in engaging and supporting them to tackle the issue. This paper recognizes the need for a pedagogical shift towards personalized learning experience to address the shortcomings of traditional teaching approaches. It aims to develop a personalized learning system named Codecaster Odyssey that caters to the diverse needs of learners. It also aims to leverage the intrinsic appeal of gaming to enhance student engagement and foster sustained interest in learning programming by integrating serious game into the learning system.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Method for Automatic Fruit Fly Detection and Counting
abstract: Fruit flies are a major threat faced by snake fruit farmers. Fruit flies can degrade the quality of snake fruits and reduce the overall yield. Traps stuffed with Methyl Eugenol are commonly placed across snake fruit plantations to attract fruit flies. Farmers then manually counted and reported the trapped fruit flies as part of their pest management strategies. However, manually counting trapped fruit flies is time-consuming, leading to unwillingness among farmers to perform this task. This study aims to develop an automated detection and counting system using deep-learning-based methods to address this issue. The proposed system was built on a modified YOLOv5 algorithm, achieving a precision of 0.944, recall of 0.947, and mAP of 0.946, with an object-counting time of only 50 ms. These results demonstrate that the proposed fruit-fly detection and counting system offers excellent performance with rapid detection times

articleTitle: PolROV (Polman Education Platform of Underwater Robot) Monitoring Navigation Design Using PID Controller Method
abstract: Underwater robots known as Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROV) have become a key element in ocean exploration and various sectors, such as marine science, underwater surveying and defense technology. In domestic research and development efforts for underwater robots, a number of research efforts have been carried out, including the development of ROVs equipped with sensors to measure specific variables such as using the MS5803-14 pressure sensor to determine water depth. Currently, ROV movement control often uses Fuzzy Logic controllers and proportional-integral-derivative (PID) methods, but ROV movement is still limited and difficult to control so that it remains stable in one place. This research aims to improve ROV navigation accuracy and ensure instructions are fulfilled. To achieve this goal, researchers designed a Raspberry Pi-based ROV that is integrated with the LabVIEW interface with the MQTT protocol as data communication between raspberry pi and LabVIEW. ROV depth control uses a dynamic diving system with a Brushless DC motor and PID control. The LabVIEW interface is used to change parameters and monitor the system during underwater ROV operation, achieving 97.06% depth measurement accuracy and 87.7% pressure sensor accuracy for navigating vertical position, resulting in an overall accuracy of 92.38%. PID simulations showed that the optimal tuning of $\text{K p}=1.5$, $\text{K i}=0.8$, and $\text{K d}=0.4$.

articleTitle: Aesthetics in Mobile Apps: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Mobile app development has witnessed rapid growth, with aesthetics playing a pivotal role in user experience and app success. This paper aims to conduct a systematic literature review to identify and analyze the key aesthetic factors influencing mobile app design. Through a comprehensive review of existing research, we aim to contribute to a deeper understanding of the relationship between aesthetics and user experience in the mobile app context. By employing a systematic literature review methodology, we systematically searched and analyzed relevant academic literature. Our review focused on identifying the predominant aesthetic factors discussed in the literature, examining their significance in mobile app design, and exploring their impact on user experience. The findings of this review highlight the importance of aesthetic factors in mobile app development. Our analysis further emphasizes the critical role of aesthetics in enhancing user engagement, satisfaction, and perceived quality. The results of this study have implications for both user experience research and the mobile app industry. By providing a clearer understanding of the aesthetic factors that drive user engagement, this research can inform the development of more effective and visually appealing mobile apps. Additionally, our findings can contribute to the development of guidelines and best practices for mobile app designers, ensuring that aesthetic considerations are integrated into the design process from the outset.

articleTitle: Fostering Innovativeness in the Automotive Industry through Digital Leadership, Citizenship, and Transformation
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of Digital Leadership, Digital Citizenship, and Digital Transformation on Innovativeness in the automotive industry. This study uses a survey method with primary data collection from employees and customers of the automotive industry. The independent variables in this study are Digital Leadership, Digital Citizenship, and Digital Transformation, while the dependent variable is Innovativeness. The sample of this study consists of employee who works at automotive industry by taking a sample of 284 respondent. To find out how the independent variables affect the dependent variable, quantitative research will be used to analyze the data collected. It is hoped that the study will increase understanding of the importance of Digital Leadership, Digital Citizenship, and Digital Transformation in increasing Innovativeness at automotive industry.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of User Acceptance Mobile E-Learning Continuing Medical Education Using Modification TAM 2 and ECT
abstract: Doctor-to-Doctor (D2D) is a mobile application and website designed for doctors and medical students. D2D offers continuous learning programs called Mobile Learning Continuing Medical Education (Mobile Learning CME). D2D has many features that make it easier for doctors to update their knowledge about the world of medicine. One of the latest features, the Medstalk Discussion Forum, is crucial for doctors to discuss daily medical cases. However, this feature does not receive sufficient user traffic or daily active users to meet expectations based on stickiness rate metric. Based on these problems, investigate has to be conducted to determine what factors influence this feature to have good acceptance from doctors. To address this issue, research was conducted using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM 2) and Expectation Confirmation Theory (ECT). The study was conducted by filling out a questionnaire with 200 user participants using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results of this study show that Job Relevance, Result Demonstrability, Content Quality and Categorization needs to be further developed based on the Medstalk feature.

articleTitle: Interpretable Machine Learning for Complex Human Activity Recognition: A Voting Classifier Approach Using AdaBoost and Random Forest
abstract: Human activity recognition is a challenging task due to various factors, such as background clutter, partial occlusion, changes in scale, viewpoint, lighting, and appearance. Moreover, the way that humans perform an activity depends on their habits, making it difficult to identify the underlying activity. This paper presents a novel approach to improve the accuracy of complex activity recognition using accelerometer-embedded mobile phone classifiers. The proposed method employs a voting technique that combines the outputs of multiple classifiers to enhance recognition accuracy while maintaining model interpretability. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a comprehensive evaluation was conducted using publicly available datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed voting-based ensemble method significantly improved the accuracy of complex activity recognition compared to individual classifiers and deep learning model. The combination of multiple machine learning models, including AdaBoost and Random Forest achieved higher recognition rates for complex activities than any single classifier alone.

articleTitle: A Survey of Quantization Techniques for Physical Layer-Based Secret Key Generation in IoT Systems
abstract: Wireless communication systems are becoming increasingly important in our daily lives, especially with the rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT). Secure and reliable communication is essential for the correct functioning of critical applications and use cases such as healthcare, finance, transportation, and industrial automation. However, the growing number of connected devices introduces significant challenges to data security and privacy due to the open nature of wireless networks. While traditional encryption methods are effective, they can be resource-intensive and impractical for resource-constrained IoT environments. Physical layer security (PLS) provides a lightweight alternative by leveraging the inherent characteristics of wireless channels to generate symmetric secret keys without requiring third-party infrastructure. The PLS key generation process involves four main stages: channel sampling, quantization, reconciliation, and privacy amplification. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of existing quantization schemes, as this step plays a crucial role in determining the key generation rate (KGR) and key disagreement rate (KDR). Additionally, the paper classifies quantization methods as either lossless or lossy, providing insights into the trade-offs between security and efficiency.

articleTitle: Face Mask Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: COVID-19 virus has affected people around the world, and it is known for its potential deadly symptoms if not treated or prevented using vaccines. This virus spreads very fast and easily as it can be airborne. One of the practical methods and solutions to stop the virus from spreading is simply using facemask. However, many people tend to wear a face mask incorrectly or in a worst-case scenario they do not wear it at all. Our work proposes a way to implement a surveillance like system to identify and recognize people wearing face masks. The development of this surveillance system is in the hope that it can be used in premises so it can help the authorities identify people who is wearing facemask incorrectly. The system can detect a face mask by implementing a CNN classification algorithm. This study focuses two CNN models with different optimizers trained with an image dataset that is labelled in two different class labels where one classes identifies as people who wear facemasks correctly and the other one identifies it as people who wears facemasks incorrectly. Furthermore, parameter tuning is implemented to increase the accuracy of the CNN model. Finally, based on the tuned model’s performance, the model with the highest accuracy was selected to be used in the surveillance system. In this study, the highest accuracy is produced by the CNN model with an Adamax optimizer that achieves 99% training accuracy.

articleTitle: Decarbonised energy efficient and sustainable routing protocol for underwater communication
abstract: Underwater sensor network comprises of devices such as autonomous vehicles and sensor nodes which depend on battery for their survival. Nowadays lithium batteries have emerged as one of the technological advancements used by devices to survive for a particular period while carrying out a specific task. Sensor nodes involved in underwater communication process are lithium battery dependent which makes it burdensome to replace or recharge. However, in the era of net-zero there is a significant energy and material cost associated with the manufacturing of lithium batteries, which in turn help in raising the embedded carbon emission known as carbon footprints. The communication procedure between these sensor nodes relies on routing to be able to transfer information from bottom to surface of the water. Scale in terms of network size plays an important role in energy preservation among sensor nodes by assessing the volume of communication to the surface of the water. As a result, this paper proposes sustainable energy efficient routing protocol for underwater communication. The proposed technique will help in minimizing energy consumption in the process of route selection thereby helping the sensor nodes to consume less energy and get prolonged in the communication process. The proposed routing protocol was simulated against other conventional routing protocols. Simulation result shows the proposed routing technique performs better in terms of energy consumption and packet delivery ratio for different number of nodes there by contributing to low carbon emission which raises the carbon footprint due to sensor nodes batteries production by factories.

articleTitle: WDCLF method for Web database design
abstract: This paper presents the WDCLF (Web Declare, Conceptual, Logical, Physical) method for web database design (WDB), which has been adapted to the needs of web applications. The WDCLF extends traditional database design approaches by adding specific elements related to Web-based systems. WDCLF offers a multi-layered architecture that allows parallel development of the data model and the processing model, accelerating the design and implementation processes. The method ensures high coordination between teams, which helps to flexibly adapt to changing requirements. Key benefits of WDCLF include scalability, security and optimized performance - key factors for the efficient operation of modern web applications. WDCLF enables integration with external systems, ensuring stability and performance under load.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Superiority of Machine Learning Ensembles in Diabetes Risk Apprehension: A Granular Analytical Perspective
abstract: Diabetes is a prevalent chronic disease that significantly impacts public health, contributing to increased morbidity and healthcare costs worldwide. Accurate prediction of diabetes risk is crucial for early intervention and effective management strategies. This study evaluates the performance of seven advanced machine learning models-ExtraTrees, RandomForest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and Logistic Regression-in predicting diabetes using a comprehensive dataset of health and demographic information from 100,000 individuals. The models were assessed based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics. ExtraTrees achieved the highest accuracy of 94.26%, with a recall of 94.32% and an AUC of 98.62%, demonstrating superior performance in identifying diabetes cases. However, RandomForest also performed exceptionally well with an accuracy of 93.93% and the highest AUC of 98.70%, making it a strong alternative model. XGBoost, LightGBM, and Gradient Boosting displayed balanced performance with accuracies of 90.65%, 89.62%, and 88.54%, respectively, indicating their potential in predictive modeling. AdaBoost and Logistic Regression, while demonstrating solid performance, showed slightly lower accuracy scores of 87.03% and 86.60%, respectively. These results underscore the potential of treebased ensemble models like ExtraTrees and RandomForest for precise diabetes prediction. Future research should focus on optimizing these models and exploring their deployment in clinical settings to enhance early detection, reduce complications, and improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Comparison between Principal Component Analysis and Sparse Principal Component Analysis as Dimensional Reduction Techniques for Random Forest based High Dimensional Data Classification
abstract: Random Forest has garnered a lot of attention from various researchers among numerous classification approaches. However, Random Forest performs poorly with very high dimensional data. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Sparse Principal Component Analysis have been suggested to enhance Random Forest’s classification performance as a dimensional reduction procedure before Random Forest is implemented. Therefore, the objective of this study was to classify high dimensional data using Random Forest alone and combined Random Forest with PCA and Sparse PCA. Using a high dimensional dataset consisting of genomic data which covers gene expression under breast cancer case (BRCA) and lung cancer case (LUAD), both PCA and Sparse PCA were applied before Random Forest was used as classification method. The results show that Sparse PCA combined with Random Forest (accuracy $=99.78 \%$) performed the best as compared to Random Forest alone (accuracy $=98.39 \%$), followed by Random Forest with PCA (accuracy $=$ 92.48%). It is noted that Sparse PCA is at advantage in tackling dimensionality problems that impede classification performance in Random Forest, particularly in genomic investigations.

articleTitle: Interaction Design for Mobile Gaming Development: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Mobile gaming is an area of digital entertainment that provides platforms for social engagement, education, fun, and cognitive development. The success of mobile games is influenced by interaction design, which encompasses the user interface, usability, and user experience. This systematic review examines recent developments in interaction design approaches, usability principles, and factors affecting the uptake of interaction design in mobile gaming. Thirty primary studies, published between 2020 and 2024, were examined. In addition, the findings show that user-centered design is the most common approach, which emphasizes user participation throughout the design process. User control and freedom are highlighted as critical usability principles that emphasize the importance of users in controlling their actions and learning at their own pace. Technological factors are important for the adoption of an interaction design in mobile gaming.

articleTitle: Decision Integrated Tree: A Machine Learning Model to Predict CO2 Emission from Power Plants
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions stem from human activities like burning fossil fuels, contributing to the greenhouse effect and climate change. In the United States, the electricity generation sector is a significant emitter, primarily from coal and natural gas. Efforts to transition to cleaner energy sources aim to mitigate CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and their adverse environmental impacts (global warming, sea level rise, and disruptions to ecosystems and biodiversity). In this research, a novel approach called Decision Integrated Tree (DIT) is presented, which investigates with a large dataset, captures complex relationships, addresses non-linearity and complexity in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission data. It commences with dataset collection (containing 5094 data points and six features), followed by thorough data preparation involving cleaning, preprocessing, and feature engineering to ensure data quality. Subsequently, our proposed DIT model is applied, incorporating various techniques (ensemble methods, pruning, and regularization). Experiments evaluate the performance of the model using significant metrics including R-squared Score ($\mathbf{R}^{2}$), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). From the experiment, we obtained $\mathbf{9 8. 2 \%} \mathrm{R}^{\mathbf{2}}, \mathbf{0. 6 3 4}$ MSE, and 0.421 MAE predicting CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions from power plants. The integration of ensemble methods, feature engineering, and hybrid models within the DIT framework enhances predictive capabilities and informs decision-making in environmental policy, industry, and research. Strong performance metrics validate the model’s reliability, while a variegated large dataset enable robust predictions in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission forecasting. However, deep learning integration and more data inclusion are needed to enhance the performance of the model and applicability for future advancements in environmental modeling.

articleTitle: Saliency-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for Interpreting U-Net Semantic Segmentation of Synthetic Liquid Spray Images
abstract: Deep learning models, particularly U-Net, have been widely used for image segmentation tasks in various domains such as medical, biological, autonomous driving, and industrial applications. However, the black-box nature of these models raises public concerns about the lack of transparency and interpretability of their decision-making processes. Unlike typical static objects, the segmentation of dynamic objects from synthetic fluid datasets are more complicated as the properties like position and shape change over time. This paper investigates these issues by exploring the uses of saliency-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques such as Class Activation Mapping (CAM), Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), Grad-CAM++ and Segmentation Grad-CAM (Seg-Grad-CAM) to generate heatmap visualizations for providing insights into the prediction of U-net semantic segmentation. Using a dataset of synthetic liquid spray images, we systematically apply these techniques to visualize the model’s attention and highlights the properties and regions of the image that are influential in the model’s predictions for different classes such as lobe, ligaments and droplets. Our results demonstrate that while all techniques provide interpretable visualizations, Seg-Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ offer better localization of salient features, providing more precise explanations for U-Net’s segmentation decisions. The comparison of the results using quantitative analysis such as Pointing Game Accuracy and Mean Localization Error also indicated that Seg-Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ are more effective for interpreting complex segmentation models in liquid spray analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Affecting the Acceptance of Maternal and Child Health Monitoring (Stunting) Applications in Suburban Areas Using a Modified Technology Acceptance Model (TAM): A Case Study in Sukabumi Regency
abstract: Maternal and child health, particularly in suburban areas with limited access to healthcare services, is a critical public health issue. One of the significant challenges is stunting, where Indonesia has a prevalence rate of 30.8%, higher than Thailand (10.5%) and Malaysia (20.7%). In Sukabumi Regency, the stunting prevalence reaches 27.5%, indicating ongoing challenges in addressing maternal and child health. This study analyses the factors influencing the adoption of maternal and child health monitoring applications by homemakers in suburban areas as part of stunting prevention efforts. The method used is a modified Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), which evaluates Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use, Content and System Quality, and User Experience. Data were collected through a questionnaire given to 262 respondents at Posyandu, using a 4-point Likert scale, and analysed with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using the Partial Least Square (PLS) technique. The research results show that content, system quality, and user experience significantly affect perceived usefulness and ease of use.Additionally, these factors positively influence behavioural intention to use the health monitoring application. The model demonstrates predictive solid power, with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values of 0.715 for Behavioral Intention, 0.758 for Perceived Usefulness, and 0.797 for Attitude Toward Using. The study concludes that improving system and content quality and user experience is essential to increasing the adoption of maternal and child health applications to support stunting reduction programs in suburban areas.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Emerging Trends of Dark Web Marketplaces and Forums
abstract: This paper investigates the evolving landscape of dark web marketplaces and forums, emphasizing their cyclical rise and fall, the resilience of their admins and users, also the security aspects that influence platform trust and longevity. Through an analysis of prominent platforms such as Abacus, Archetyp, and Cypher, the study traces patterns of user migration in response to other dark web marketplace closures and highlights the role of illicit forums as a hub communication between every dark web user. In addition, dark web forums such as BreachForums, XSS, and Altenen are explored for their role in facilitating cybercrime. While this research primarily relies on secondary data, it identifies key trends that inform future research directions. To address the limitations of current dark web data collection, this paper advocates for the development of more sophisticated web crawlers and advances in dark web forensics to better analyze encrypted communications and illicit activities.

articleTitle: Electric Mobility Vehicle Reservation and Crowd Management for Al-masjid Al-haram
abstract: This paper addresses the growing need for efficient management of electric mobility vehicles in high-traffic environments. We present the design and development of a software system to support electric mobility vehicle reservation and management for use in the existence of crowds. The design is applied on a use case for electric vehicles used by visitors to Al-masjid Al-haram for performing “Tawaf”, a pilgrimage ritual conducted by Muslims visiting the holy land in Makkah. To enhance accessibility for visitors, the government has introduced electric mobility vehicles. However, the current manual reservation and management poses challenges, including locating the vehicles, unpredictable waiting times, the lack of real-time vehicle availability information, and congestions. The design of the software solution aims to address these challenges using automated reservation and management, heatmap crowd detection, and location-based GPS to track and locate vehicles. A preliminary evaluation on a sample of target users indicates the usefulness of the system and its ability to contribute to solving current management problems and enhancing the experience of visitors.

articleTitle: Identifying Completeness Issues in Unstructured Social Media Data for Business Insights: Data Usability Perspective
abstract: Social media data has become a vital source of information for businesses, offering diverse insights through various media formats. Text, in particular, holds significant potential for providing valuable information. However, the large volume of text data often exists in an unstructured form, posing challenges for extracting maximum value due to usability issues. Improving the usability of unstructured social media data is essential for organisations to gain deeper market insights and make more informed decisions. The existing literature identifies different types of usability dimensions from unstructured big data such as availability, completeness and relevance- To the best of our knowledge, existing literature lacks a comprehensive investigation of challenges for one particular usability dimension. This research aims to address this gap by conducting a systematic literature review to identify the issues of completeness dimension for unstructured social media data in the business domain. The findings of this study will assist researchers in overcoming these challenges and optimising the extraction of meaningful insights from unstructured social media data.

articleTitle: A Derived Framework for Immersive Analytics: Use Cases in Smart City and Pokémon Interactive Data Visualization
abstract: Immersive analytics (IA) explores the use of immersive technologies to enhance data visualization and interaction. To maximize the potential of IA, it is essential to develop effective and practical applications. In this context, an IA design framework plays a crucial role as it provides a structured approach to define user requirements and guide the development of the application. This paper proposed a design framework for IA, adapted from several established works. The framework was applied to two use cases: visualizing smart city data in a virtual reality environment and Pokémon data in a mixed reality environment. These use cases demonstrate the applicability of the framework in guiding the development of IA applications that can be used to perform various tasks in different immersive settings and domains. Besides, a user study was conducted with 30 participants to assess their perceived workload while interacting with these applications. Future work will focus on conducting more comprehensive evaluations in terms effectiveness and efficiency to provide insights for further enhancements.

articleTitle: Towards Digital Twin Integrated Border Control
abstract: As a promising enabling technology for digital transformation with the prime goal of solving numerous challenges, digital twin concept has gained significant recognition among researchers and practitioners, and has been adopted across many different industries. The importance of data to digital twin cannot be overstated. Data plays a critical role in constructing virtual models, building cyber-physical connections, and executing intelligent operations. Driven by data and model, the digital twin modeling is the core for accurate portrayal of its physical entity, which enables the digital twin to deliver a functional service in monitoring and prediction. Against this background, the paper suggests the adoption of digital twin within the border control domain for risk monitoring purposes. The monitoring function will identify, analyze, and respond to illegal activities at national entry points. The virtual data is collected from various sources of IoT devices. This research conducts a thorough review of existing literature and analysis on technology advancements to present the emerging trends and technology used in border control and subsequently proposed a model and framework of digital twin integrated border control that will support risk monitoring of border authority. Exploratory investigation was conducted in search for model and framework validation. Result of the survey shows that the majority of the respondents agreed with the idea of digital twin implementation within border control domain to support risk monitoring. The preliminary study proved that digital twin integration contributes to the effectiveness and efficiency of border protection routine.

articleTitle: Enhancing Rice Yield Prediction using Vision Transformer and Regression Models
abstract: Amidst the growing global population, complex dynamics of climate change, and challenges in agricultural economies, ensuring food security and supporting agricultural policy planning have become more critical than ever. Thus, predicting rice yield before the harvest season is essential for billions who rely on rice as a staple food. In this study, we propose a novel approach for predicting rice yield using images of rice fields captured at the ripening stage. Our proposal leverages the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture’s ability to extract relevant features from field images for yield prediction. Consequently, we replace the classification layer in the original ViT model with a regression layer to predict numerical values of rice yield. To determine the most effective regression method, we trained a variety of regression techniques. In an effort to develop a rice-specific prediction model for the Mekong Delta, we collected over 11,000 RGB images from 47 plots, encompassing more than 28 hectares in An Giang and Tra Vinh provinces, using digital cameras, smartphones, and fixed-wing UAVs. The rough grain yield recorded after harvest in these areas ranged from 6 to 12 tons per hectare (t/ha). Experimental results demonstrated that the ensemble regression model based on ViT achieved the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) of 72.72, underscoring the potential of ViT in agricultural yield forecasting.

articleTitle: Exploring Non-Functional Requirements in Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Review
abstract: Non-functional requirements (NFRs) are often poorly documented and inadequately integrated into the software development process resulting in discrepancies between expected and actual system quality. This gap leads to a number of issues like requirement ambiguity, ineffective stakeholder communication and inadequate validation which severely impact project outcomes. This systematic review addresses these challenges by investigating the state of NFRs management in requirements engineering. The review identifies predominant techniques such as automated tools and document analysis for eliciting NFRs while also highlighting current challenges and effective validation practices, including inspections, reviews and user feedback. Future research should develop comprehensive frameworks combining technology with human-centered approaches to address these challenges.

articleTitle: MIMOS Independent Verification &Validation (IV&V) as an Enabler for Information Technologies Companies to Improve ESG Ratings and Market Value
abstract: Despite the high growth by the Bursa Malaysia Technology sector, the level of sustainability for continuous growth is at risk of being excluded from supplying their services to Multinational Companies. The Carbon Transition is crucial as per the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, climate change is reaching urgency level whereby globally we are not on track to prevent the temperature increase by $1.5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ that will impact nature and the human system. To address these problems and to support these efforts, the first objective of this paper is to identify requirements for the environment, social and governance (ESG) for companies in Malaysia. The second objective of this paper is to compare related research, development and services (case studies) by the MIMOS IV&V against the ESG requirement (objective 1).The mixed research methodology employed in this paper includes secondary data analysis such as a poll and expert interviews. Subject matter experts from MIMOS IV&V were interviewed to identify case studies (if any) to gauge the readiness to serve and fulfill the ESG requirements. Based on these, 12 selected IV&V case studies were identified and comparison of these case studies against the ESG requirements were carried out. Finally, recommendation are put forward together with the proposed MIMOS IV&V Framework to help improve the ESG ratings and thus the market value of the companies in Malaysia towards attaining sustainable growth.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Risk-Based Access Control Models for IoT: Balancing Security, Adaptability, and Resource Efficiency
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized how devices connect and interact, but it also brings serious security challenges, especially in managing access control. Traditional models like Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) often fall short in the face of IoT’s dynamic and complex environments. This paper offers a comprehensive analysis of 14 risk-based access control models, evaluated across five key criteria: security effectiveness, scalability, resource efficiency, adaptability, and integration of AI and machine learning. Advanced models leveraging AI, fuzzy logic, and neuro-fuzzy systems demonstrate exceptional accuracy and adaptability but face many other resource demands and scalability challenges. Conversely, resource-efficient models often trade off security and adaptability. Our findings underscore the need for innovative hybrid solutions that balance these competing priorities. This study provides practical insights for IoT practitioners and policymakers while highlighting research gaps to inspire future advancements in risk-based access control for IoT systems.

articleTitle: The Comparison of Survival Right Censored Log-Logistic Models for Breast Cancer Bootstrap Data
abstract: Breast cancer is a significant global health concern, with increasing incidence and mortality rates particularly affecting women worldwide. In Malaysia, limited data exists on how survival rates vary across different age groups, despite evidence that breast cancer behavior differs by age. Due to time constraints, this study only included data from 32 patients and five variables. This study addresses the gap by examining survival rates in two age groups of breast cancer patients from Johor, Malaysia, using right-censored data from 32 women treated at Hospital Sultan Ismail. The cutoff point of $\mathbf{5 2}$ years is based on the mean age of the dataset, which helps simplify the analysis while ensuring meaningful comparison within the available data. Due to limited data, bootstrapping methods were employed to address small sample sizes, while survival analysis, specifically the Kaplan-Meier method, was used to assess survival patterns. Contrary to previous findings, older patients showed a higher probability of survival. The accuracy of bootstrapping method was validated through coverage probability, which exceeded $70 \%$ for all datasets. The log-logistic model with 100 replications was the best fit based on statistical measures like AIC, BIC, and p-values. Despite no significant interactions between variables, this study highlights the need for further research with additional variables and parametric models to improve breast cancer survival analysis in Malaysia

articleTitle: CluckTrack: Manok Bisaya Monitor using Computer Vision Yolo V8 and IOT GSM Alert for Sustainable Farming
abstract: CluckTrack is an advanced system designed for real-time surveillance and management of chickens within a coop environment. It utilizes the YOLOv8s algorithm for object detection, leveraging an ESP32-CAM to capture images and videos, which are transmitted via WiFi to a Firebase database for processing and storage. The ESP32-CAM is powered directly by a power bank. An Arduino Uno, connected directly to a computer, manages the SIM800C GSM module, facilitating cellular connectivity for remote monitoring. In the event of a missing or inactive chicken, Firebase triggers a notification to the GSM module, which sends an SMS alert to the user. The system was evaluated using a custom dataset of 118 annotated images of Manok Bisaya chickens, demonstrating impressive performance metrics, including a precision of 92.8%, recall of 93.9%, mean Average Precision (mAP) of 95.3%, overall accuracy of 82%, and an F1 score of 93.3%. The YOLOv8s algorithm showed satisfactory performance with minimal missed detections, averaging an inference time of 0.9739 seconds per image. The Flutter-based app offers functionalities such as viewing the image gallery, updating contact information, checking the number of chickens in the coop, and receiving notifications. Recommendations for future improvements include expanding the dataset, upgrading the camera and microcontroller, integrating single-board computers for on-device processing, and adding WiFi configuration capabilities in the app. CluckTrack provides a robust solution for farmers, enabling efficient management of their flocks through advanced image recognition, real-time notifications, and a user-friendly interface.

articleTitle: Lightweight Deep Learning-Based Network Traffic Classification Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: To address the growing demand for internet usage and connected devices, it is essential to implement robust Network Traffic Classification (NTC) methods that guarantee network security and optimised resource utilisation. Deep learning approaches are continuously gaining traction due to their capabilities in learning complex network traffic patterns and effective classification. However, the performance of deep learning (DL) approaches comes with the cost of huge computational resources that struggle to perform under a resource-constrained environment. Therefore, this study proposes enhancing DL-based NTC by integrating an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) technique, the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), to identify and select the most important features. This study leverages the explainability of XAI to enhance model performance and optimise resource utilisation through feature selection. To evaluate the selected features, this paper compares three algorithms, which are Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), using the ISCXVPN2016 dataset on an NVIDIA Tesla T4. The result shows a $\mathbf{1 2 . 4 2 \%}, \mathbf{1 0 . 7 2 \%}$, and $\mathbf{1 0 . 2 3 \%}$ decrease in RAM usage for MLP, CNN, and GRU, respectively, while reducing the GPU memory usage by $6 \%$ and an improvement up to $4.99 \%$ F1-score compared to the state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review on the Use of Digital Technologies in Outdoor Education
abstract: In the past, there were discrepancies in the use of digital technologies in outdoor education (OE) where the experts of OEE contested over the idea that digital technologies may hinder the authentic experience of the participants in the outdoors. However, studies have been conducted to describe more structured ways that digital technologies can be used outdoors to enhance experience and learning. This research examines and analyzes publications on the application of digital technologies in outdoor education spanning from 2020 to 2024. It investigates four research inquiries pertaining to the contemporary trends in research methodologies, assessment techniques, contributions, and correlations among them. After employing a filtering process, the research has identified 40 pertinent papers. This article will initially showcase all descriptive findings, data analyses, correlations, and, finally, insights from the review analysis processes.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Traffic Congestion Prediction Models: Machine Learning and Statistical Approaches
abstract: Traffic congestion prediction has become a critical component of intelligent transportation systems, enabling more efficient traffic management and urban planning. This study provides an in-depth review and analysis of the most recent methodologies applied to traffic congestion prediction, including machine learning, statistical, and hybrid models. We evaluate key studies that demonstrate how machine learning models excel at handling non-linear traffic patterns and real-time data processing, while statistical models, remain useful in stable and predictable environments. Hybrid models, which combine the strengths of both approaches, show promise in improving prediction accuracy and managing uncertainties. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges of scalability, generalizability, and the integration of external factors such as weather and accidents. Based on these findings, we propose several future directions for traffic congestion prediction research. The review highlights the necessity of further refining these methodologies to develop more adaptable and efficient predictive systems for modern urban environments.

articleTitle: Development and Assessment of Carlos Hilado Memorial State University (CHMSU) Learning and Assessment Management System
abstract: The rapid integration of Information and Communication Technology has revolutionized education, with Learning Management Systems (LMS) becoming essential for supporting modern teaching and learning processes. However, traditional LMS platforms often fail to align with OutcomeBased Education (OBE) requirements, particularly in tracking and assessing specific competencies that align educational outcomes with industry standards. This study addresses this gap by developing the Carlos Hilado Memorial State University Learning and Assessment Management System (CLAMS), which maps educational content and assessments directly to OBE competencies. CLAMS was developed using the Iterative Development Model, which involved multiple design, development, and testing cycles. The system includes an integrated virtual classroom and assessment manager, evaluated based on the ISO/IEC 25010:2011 standards for software quality, focusing on key attributes such as functionality, usability, reliability, and security. Using a developmental and descriptive design, usability data were gathered from faculty, students, and IT experts through purposive sampling. Results indicate that CLAMS successfully integrates OBE principles, enhances student performance in competency-based assessments, and receives high usability and acceptability scores. The findings suggest that CLAMS is a robust, scalable, and user-friendly platform for improving educational outcomes, making it a valuable tool for institutions adopting OBE frameworks.

Author Keywords: CHMSU Learning and Assessment Management System (CLAMS)

articleTitle: Two-Stage Feature Selection for PM2.5 Prediction: adjcor-TRBFNN Approach to Address Multicollinearity in Air Quality Data in Urban Area
abstract: PM2.5 is a dangerous pollutant that has been shown to significantly affect human health due to its small size ($\leq 2.5$ micrometers). Urban areas often experience higher PM2.5 levels due to high traffic volume, industrial activities, and population density. Accurate prediction of PM2.5 levels not only enhances the body of knowledge on air quality modeling but also provides governments with critical insights to implement timely interventions, reduce public health risks, and guide policymaking for air quality management. Thus, this study aims to classify the next day’s air quality based on PM2.5 levels in Banting, an urban area in Selangor, Malaysia, using a machine learning approach. Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) is a neural network method widely used for prediction and classification analysis due to it can handle complex nonlinear relationship in the dataset. However, RBFNN does not address multicollinearity in air quality data. To address this, we used the adjcorT feature selection method to identify the significant features affecting next-day PM2.5 levels, while considering the multicollinearity issues in air quality data. Thus, a two-stage feature selection method, adjcorT-RBFNN, was implemented in this study to enhance the classification of nextday PM2.5 levels. The research utilized hourly secondary data from the Department of Environment Malaysia (DOE), spanning 2018 to 2022. The findings indicate that PM10, PM2.5, CO, NO2, humidity, SO2, wind speed, and wind direction are significant features for classifying next-day PM2.5 levels in Banting. Moreover, the proposed adjcorT-RBFNN technique outperformed the RBFNN method in terms of accuracy, specificity, precision, F1 score, and AUROC, with scores of $0.761,0.752,0.752,0.761$, and 0.761, respectively. Hence, the proposed two-stage feature selection method, adjcorT-RBFNN, can assist future researchers in improving PM2.5 level predictions in other urban areas.

articleTitle: ThomaSIGHTS: Evaluating Nursery Students’ Learning Styles through Body Language and Engagement
