abstract: Identifying diverse learning styles in early childhood education is a significant challenge that can hinder academic progress. To address this, this study presents ThomaSIGHTS, a system developed to analyze nursery students’ body language and engagement for effective learning style prediction. The system utilizes YOLO and DeepSORT algorithms for body language detection, the Random Forest algorithm to predict the percentages of visual, auditory, and kinesthetic learning styles, and Hybrid Filtering to suggest tailored teaching approaches. Evaluations conducted through a survey involving IT professionals and nursery teachers, adhering to ISO/IEC 25010 standards, resulted in high scores for Functional Suitability (4.17), Usability (4.35), Reliability (4.33), and Performance Efficiency (4.36). Additionally, the system achieved an mean precision of 82.08% an average recall of 59.42%, an average F1 score of 68.25%, an overall accuracy of 62.17%, and an average precision (AP) of 79.5%. The confusion matrix results indicated the identification of 4,305 true positives and 3,195 true negatives, demonstrating strong classification capabilities, although 2,272 false positives and 917 false negatives revealed areas for improvement. These findings demonstrate that ThomaSIGHTS is a reliable tool for detecting students’ body language, predicting learning styles percentages, and suggesting tailored teaching approaches, thereby enhancing classroom engagement and addressing the educational needs of nursery students.

articleTitle: Real-Time Recycle Waste Classification Using Deep Learning: A Convolutional Neural Network Model for Automated Waste Management
abstract: The advancement of segregation of recycle waste classification applications has been increased by the development of innovative solutions which utilise modern technologies for effective waste management and recycling practices. However, there have problems when most of the country are lack of garbage collection and mechanism facilities, traditional waste management is inefficient and costly, and most people are not aware of how to manage recycle waste correctly. Therefore, this paper presents and studies a smart recycle waste classification of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to automate the real-time recyclable waste classification for three types of waste such as metal, paper, plastic. Four phases that applied in this study which are data acquisition, pre-processing, processing (i.e CNN architecture model), and post-processing (i.e test and evaluation). A total of 3000 images have been experimented in this study. All image datasets have been captured in Malacca and collected from the Garbage Classification and Waste Segregation Image Dataset. The CNN architecture model has been applied in this study. To evaluate the quantitative predictive performance of the proposed model, confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are computed with random-splitting and manual-splitting of train-test image dataset with the ratio of $70: 30,80: 20$, and $90: 10$. The results of this study showed the highest rate of $97.30 \%$: $93.67 \%$, $\mathbf{9 7 . 3 0 \%}$: 93.67%, $\mathbf{9 7 . 3 6 \%}$: 96.24%, and 97.26%: 96.18% for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, respectively. Thus, it for is hoped to streamline waste sorting procedures and enable effective recycling techniques to deploy the smart recycle waste classification system, and significantly influence waste management initiatives, fostering sustainability and environmental protection. For the future work, this study may extend to experiment the other various type of recycle waste and experimented for various machine learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive Upsampling and Optimal Parameterization of Support Vector Machine for Enhanced Face Recognition in Resnet-based Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Face recognition has advanced significantly due to deep learning, primarily via libraries like Dlib. This paper proposes adaptive upsampling in the Residual Network (ResNet)-34 deep learning architecture to improve face detection in low-resolution images. The Support Vector Machine (SVM) is integrated into the fully connected layers classification tasks to improve accuracy. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduces feature dimensions, reducing training time and increasing detection rate. ResNet-34 in Dlib is trained using 128 face feature vectors and Euclidean distance on the Labeled Faces in the Wild (LFW) dataset. Reducing PCA dimensions from $\mathbf{1 0 0}$ to $\mathbf{5 0}$ or SVM cost parameters from 100 to 50 has no noticeable impact on accuracy. Still, it gives more Frame Per Second (FPS) in real-time recognition because the parameters are fewer.

articleTitle: Recondite Thyroid Pathology Prediction: Hermeneutic Integration of Neural and Machine Learning Architectures
abstract: Thyroid issues are increasingly prevalent, making early detection crucial for reducing mortality and complications. Accurate disease progression estimation and understanding clinical feature interactions are essential for effective medical diagnosis and treatment. Our study addresses these challenges by employing machine learning and deep learning models with advanced clinical feature analysis and ensemble-learning techniques. This approach aids in predicting disease progression and assessing the interdependence of clinical features. We utilized five models-K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), XGBoost, Random Forest, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and TabNet-to identify the best thyroid prediction outcomes. Our experimental results indicate that the proposed models significantly outperform traditional methods. The CNN model achieved the highest accuracy ($\mathbf{9 8. 7 0 \%}$) and AUC ($\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$), followed by TabNet with an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7. 4 0 \%}$ and AUC of $\mathbf{9 9. 1 8 \%}$, demonstrating superior performance in complex classification tasks. The ensemble ML classifier combining multiple models achieved $100 \%$ sensitivity and $\mathbf{9 9. 7 1 \%}$ accuracy. By effectively addressing feature reduction and high-class imbalance, our ensemble approach excels in handling classification challenges, confirming its effectiveness in thyroid disease prediction.

articleTitle: Assessment Analysis of Data Ticketing Quality of The Multimedia Division of Telecommunication Companies in Indonesia Using Data Quality Assessment (DQA) Based on DAMA-DMBOK
abstract: Many companies have not implemented good data quality as a process carried out consistently so problems arise. These problems can be reduced by implementing good data quality management. One of the processes in data quality management is data quality assessment (DQA). This study focuses on analyzing and assessing data quality using a methodology related to DQA techniques and guidelines designed based on the DAMA-DMBOK framework. This study focuses on determining the dataset on the ticketing business process of the multimedia division of telecommunication companies in Indonesia. In the analysis process, the author justifies with a null error on the data and performs an objective or quantitative assessment with DQ dimensions, namely accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, and validity. In justifying the ticketing data, the author gets an accumulated null error of $66.23 \%$ which when judged there are still many discrepancies with the DQ dimension. At the improvement stage, the writer gives suggestions for improvements to the ERD ticketing process, provides suggestions that can be made based on the DQ dimension, and performs data treatment as handling null data which can be filled in, because ticketing data is impossible to delete.

articleTitle: Developing Deep Learning Models to Predict Benign and Malicious Attacks in IoT Networks

abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has afforded increased connectivity across various domains which increased cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Threats like Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, Spoofing, and web-based attacks pose a significant danger to IoT networks, which require more advanced Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) to effectively counter these threats. The aim of this paper is to investigate the viability of DL-based classifiers for NIDS. The CICIoT2023 dataset is used in this study. Feature reduction is performed using the Pearson’s Correlation Coefficient (PCC) Matrix and features that contain all-zero values are removed. To resolve the class imbalanced issue, Synthetic Minority Oversampling (SMOTE) is applied exclusively on the training set only. For comprehensive comparison studies, a total of nine classifiers have been considered which can be categorized into machine learning (ML)-based classifiers and Deep Learning (DL)-based classifiers. MLbased classifiers consist of Random Forest (RF), Naive Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Logistic Regression (LR), and while DL-based classifiers consist of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory (BiLSTM), 1-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN). The findings revealed that the DL-based classifiers have consistently recorded high accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and AUC of more than 0.9. Although ML-based classifiers have recorded high precision and AUC, the accuracy, recall and F1 score have a wider variation in scores. The consistency and high scores across various evaluation metrics indicate the viability of adopting DL-based classifiers for building NIDS.

articleTitle: Rainfall Prediction based on Time-series Data and Temporal Convolutional Network for Flood Forecasting in Malaysia
abstract: Extreme rainfall can lead to flood disasters that bring detrimental impacts on various aspects of human lives. Rainfall forecasting is a sophisticated time-series problem due to its nonlinear nature. Recently, deep learning algorithms, such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), have appeared as effective approaches to handling time-series data. However, LSTM has limitations in dealing with long-distance dependencies. Therefore, this study aims to present a deep learning model based on Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to address the problem of LSTM in forecasting rainfall amounts for flood prediction. The proposed model was trained and tested using observed rainfall data from multiple states in Malaysia. The performance of the proposed solution was benchmarked with various baseline architectures, including Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Bidirectional GRU (BiGRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM). Several evaluation metrics were used to assess the performance of the proposed model, such as Mean Square Error (MSE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination ($\mathbf{R}^{2}$). Results from the comparative experiments indicated that TCN outperformed other deep learning models, achieving the lowest MSE, RMSE, and MAE scores of 0.0050, 0.0706, and 0.1467, respectively. The model also obtained the highest $R^{2}$ value of 0.8592, indicating that TCN can effectively handle time-series data and provide accurate prediction of rainfall amounts.

articleTitle: Discrepancy and Thematic Bibliometric Analyses of the Remaining Limitations in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) advances, it is essential to continuously comprehend its limitations to optimise the integration of AI into autonomous systems that empower humans. The first objective of this study is to highlight the key capabilities of both humans and AI, focusing on the differences and identifying limitations of AI from the literature. Through discrepancy analysis, this study uses a Venn diagram to visualise the remaining limitations of AI into five key domains: (i) emotional intelligence, (ii) consciousness and awareness, (iii) creative imagination, (iv) communication, and (v) ethical decision-making. Furthermore, this study employs thematic bibliometric analysis to provide a more detailed examination of each AI limitation as the second objective. This study has identified underdeveloped and emerging research themes with potential for future development, such as emotion recognition, human-computer interaction, digital health, and situational awareness, which may require further research. Additionally, this study commends the ongoing efforts to harness AI’s computational power and algorithmic innovations to enhance AI’s overall performance and applicability.

articleTitle: Improved the Accuracy of Indoor Positioning at the Meter Level in Large and Complex Environments Through AI-Powered Sensor Fusion
abstract: Indoor positioning systems (IPS) continue to encounter significant challenges in achieving meter-level accuracy, particularly in large and intricate environments such as airports, hospitals, and industrial sites. Despite substantial advancements in technologies like Wi-Fi Fine Time Measurement (FTM), Ultra-Wideband (UWB), and 5G, their scalability and precision often suffer in dynamic, obstacle-laden settings. To enhance accuracy and adaptability, this study presents an innovative AI-driven sensor fusion technique that integrates machine learning models with various positioning technologies. This study achieves significant improvements in positioning accuracy through dynamic sensor input adjustments and real-time environmental awareness. Additionally, this study also includes results from a thorough evaluation of the system’s effectiveness across diverse practical applications, while exploring its potential uses within the Internet of Things (IoT) framework.

articleTitle: Optimizing Edge Computing Usability with Random Forest Algorithms
abstract: This study convincingly demonstrates the immense potential of Random Forest algorithms to significantly enhance usability in edge computing environments by concentrating on critical parameters such as execution time, energy consumption, and scalability. By leveraging the power of the Random Forest technique, we train models using a multitude of decision trees, which not only improves prediction accuracy but also effectively combats overfitting. This approach directly addresses pressing challenges, including limited resources, scalability issues, and the unpredictability of network conditions. Our results are impressive: we achieved a noteworthy reduction in mean execution time by 0.73 seconds and a standard deviation of 1.15 seconds. These metrics highlight the model’s remarkable resilience and reliability in boosting system responsiveness. With these advancements, Random Forest stands out as a formidable solution for the demanding real-time processing needs inherent in edge computing. Our research presents a compelling strategy for establishing robust and effective edge computing infrastructures by closing crucial gaps that currently exist, particularly the lack of scalable solutions for large, heterogeneous edge platforms, adaptability in fluctuating contexts, and real-world validation. In summary, our work lays a solid foundation for further exploration of adaptive Random Forest applications that can seamlessly adjust to dynamic network conditions, reinforcing the significance of edge computing in latency-sensitive, nextgeneration applications.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques with Self-Attention Mechanisms for Enhanced Macroeconomic Trend Forecasting in BRICS Nations
abstract: Accurate forecasting of macroeconomic trends is crucial for informed policy-making in the dynamic economies of BRICS nations; yet, traditional methods struggle to capture complex temporal dynamics, such as non-linear relationships and long-range dependencies. This paper proposes a novel hybrid framework that integrates transformer architectures with ARIMA models to effectively forecast macroeconomic trends. By combining transformers to capture long-term dependencies with ARIMA for short-term temporal patterns, our hybrid approach offers a comprehensive and robust forecasting solution. The model incorporates domain-specific economic knowledge, such as the impacts of fiscal policy on inflation, to enhance accuracy. Evaluated on a comprehensive dataset of key economic indicators from BRICS countries, empirical results indicate significant improvements in forecasting accuracy over traditional models, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid approach. Additionally, an attention analysis was conducted to understand the internal mechanisms of the model, providing insights into the importance of various economic indicators over time and enhancing model transparency and interpretability. This research contributes to economic analysis by presenting a robust methodology that integrates domain expertise with advanced machine learning techniques, thereby improving macroeconomic forecasting accuracy in emerging markets.

articleTitle: Predicting Hypernasality Using Spectrogram Via Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN)
abstract: Hypernasality, marked by excessive nasal resonance during a speech, impairs communication clarity, particularly for sounds requiring soft palate closure, such as the “f” in ‘football’. Common causes include cleft lip and palate, velopharyngeal insufficiency, neurological disorders, adenoid issues, anatomical defects, and nerve system impairments. Detection and management in clinical settings are challenging due to the limited availability of speech-language pathologists (SLPs), subjective evaluation methods, and inefficient workflows. This study uses a speech feature with a deep learning model to predict the hypernasality in individuals. The objective of the study is to reduce reliance on SLPs, ensure consistent and objective evaluations, and enhance clinical efficiency. The study achieved a $\mathbf{9 2 . 3 1 \%}$ accuracy in detecting hypernasality using the spectrogram features extraction method via Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN). The clinical can apply this study by developing a user-friendly GUI and integrating it with a secure database. Using suitable tools for deployment, this study can be effectively applied in clinical settings. The contribution of this study is that it addresses the scarcity of SLPs and enhances clinical evaluation practices, ultimately improving communication outcomes for individuals with hypernasality.

articleTitle: Advancing Cervical Cancer Risk Stratification via Ensemble Learning Models Integrated with SHAP-Based Interpretability Methods
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, particularly in regions with limited access to regular screening. Early detection improves prognosis, yet traditional methods such as Pap smears and HPV testing are often unavailable in low-resource settings. In this work, we present a novel machine learning framework for cervical cancer risk prediction, leveraging a Stacking ensemble of Gradient Boosting (GB), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), and Support Vector Machines (SVM). To address class imbalance in the dataset, we apply the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), while Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) identifies the most relevant clinical and demographic features. Model interpretability is ensured through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), providing insights into feature contributions. Our approach achieves a state-of-the-art accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9 . 0 0 \%}$, outperforming individual models and demonstrating the effectiveness of ensemble learning for early diagnosis. This work presents a scalable, interpretable, and clinically viable solution for improving cervical cancer screening in resource-constrained environments, setting a new benchmark in predictive modeling for medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Smart Braille Translator: Integrating Braille-to-Speech and Speech-to-Braille Using Raspberry Pi
abstract: In the Philippines, approximately half a million individuals are estimated to have visual impairments, with a significant number lacking the ability to read Braille. This study addresses various challenges in the development of a Braille translation system, such as ensuring accurate conversion of Braille characters into text and speech. The system leverages a Raspberry $\operatorname{Pi} 4$ as a microcontroller, employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for scanning Braille characters, followed by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Braille mapping for translation. Moreover, the study will integrate the principles of assistive technology theory throughout the development of the system. During data gathering, the proponents discovered that most respondents from the Philippine Blind Union community had only a basic understanding of Braille. The study ultimately achieved its three primary objectives by implementing the system successfully. Regarding Braille conversion, the system demonstrated a $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ accuracy rate for simple dot patterns and $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$ for more complex patterns. Additionally, the camera scanning yielded $96 \%$ accuracy in well-lit conditions and 70% accuracy in dim lighting. The final system evaluation, based on ISO 25010:2023 standards, showed positive feedback from respondents who tested the system.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches to Babylonian Numeral Recognition: A CNN-SVM Hybrid Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning framework for classifying Babylonian numerals by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with a hybrid CNN-SVM model. The core contributions include the development of a robust feature extraction pipeline combining zoning, component analysis, and angular analysis of cuneiform symbols, optimized with deep learning techniques. The proposed system extends beyond numeral classification by incorporating object recognition and counting mechanisms to accurately convert multi-digit Babylonian numbers into their decimal equivalents in the base- 60 system. This approach achieves remarkable accuracy of $98.33 \%$, significantly advancing automated recognition and interpretation of ancient mathematical symbols. By bridging machine learning with historical data analysis, the research contributes to the preservation and scholarly study of Babylonian mathematical heritage while demonstrating the efficacy of hybrid models for complex, historical numeral recognition tasks.

articleTitle: Building Flood Resilience: A 3D Simulation Game for Public Awareness
abstract: This article presents the development and evaluation of “Flood,” a 3D simulation game designed to enhance public awareness of flood safety measures. The game features two distinct phases: the Pre-flood phase, where players prepare for impending flood conditions, and the Evacuation phase, where they must navigate various hazards to reach safety. By utilizing the Unity platform, “Flood” immerses players in realistic scenarios that promote learning through engagement. Results from a survey of ${2 0}$ participants indicate that the game successfully simulates flood situations, with ${8 0 \%}$ of respondents affirming its effectiveness in conveying essential flood awareness. The majority of players reported learning crucial safety measures, such as avoiding power lines and preparing emergency bags. Furthermore, feedback highlighted high levels of engagement, with $70 \%$ rating the game at the highest level of interest.

articleTitle: Measuring the Level of LMS (Web) User Satisfaction among XYZ University Students Using the modified EUCS Method
abstract: Following the pandemic, the need for distant learning interrupted the teaching and learning process, resulting in numerous adjustments. The phenomenon has an impact on learning activities, encouraging lecturers to be more innovative in their teaching ways. This study looked at the effectiveness of teaching and learning activities using an LMS (Learning Management System) by analyzing the level of satisfaction among XYZ University students, utilizing the End-User Computing satisfaction (EUCS) model with a slight modification as a framework. The EUCS model, encompassing factors like Accuracy, Content, Ease of Use, Format, and Timeliness, is presented as the tool to measure user satisfaction. The factor of System Speed and Security is also used in this research to further examine user satisfaction. The methodology section details the sample selection process and survey instrument development based on the EUCS model.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Semantic and Ontology for Searching Disease-Related QA Answers from Online Health Consultation Texts
abstract: The inability of the search feature to find relevant information based on keywords in the set of questions (Q) and answers (A) in online health consultation (OHC) may lead to inaccurate search results. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the best method to help search engines find relevant information according to keywords, mainly Q&A containing medical text. This study aims to find a method that is significantly accurate in finding relevant information related to diseases based on the history Q&A of OHC. This study compares two methods, namely semantics and ontology. Both methods were tested, and their performance results were compared using a prototype website for searching disease-related Q.A. text that we developed. The research stages were divided into four parts, namely data selection, back-end scenarios, front-end and testing, with the research dataset in the form of a collection of doctor’s answer texts from one of the OHCs with the topic of high-risk diseases according to WHO, namely Tuberculosis (T.B.), Diarrhea, HIV/AIDS, and Kidney Stones. The results show that the ontology method is more accurate in finding disease information related to questions and answers on OHC, with a precision of 75%, recall of 100%, and F1-score of 82% compared to the semantic method.

articleTitle: Understanding Comparative Genomics Data Visualization for Biodiversity Domain Through Persona-Based Interviews
abstract: Understanding the needs of genomic data visualization techniques is important to help bioinformaticians to perform their comparative analytical tasks effectively. DNA sequencing datasets consist of a long sequential string of nucleotide base pairs combination and are often involved in multiple sequences alignment for comparative analysis. Therefore, existing challenges include designing suitable visualization layout and the need of user-centered approach to ensure optimal user experience. Existing works also featured heavily on the qualitative evaluation of comparative visualization tools, such as use cases and case studies, which are difficult to quantify and conduct follow up evaluation for tool improvement. Hence, this paper aims to understand the needs of visualization tools in comparative genomic analysis to identify visualization tasks and visual design requirements. The methodology includes the creation of semi-structured interview based on personas template as guiding questions and the synthesis of thematic analysis results. These results presented the requirements of the visualization tasks for the biodiversity domain based on comparative targets. For future work, this research will design, develop, and validate the comparative visualization tool based on the discovered requirements.

articleTitle: ForenSEEK: Gamifying Learning Experiences in Digital Forensics using Unity Engine and Augmented Reality Technology
abstract: This study focuses on developing ForenSEEK, a game-based application designed to encourage Filipino young adults (aged 18-30) to pursue careers in digital forensics or cybersecurity in response to the growing demand for these professions due to the increase in cybercrime cases in the Philippines, mainly caused by end-users’ limited cybersecurity awareness. Unlike typical 2-dimensional (2D) games, ForenSEEK integrates Augmented Reality (AR) technology and a feedback mechanism to create a more interactive and immersive learning experience in various cybercrime scenarios. Survey results from 150 young adults (113 students and 37 employees) showed significant overall knowledge improvement, from approximately 54% in the Pre-Test to 77% in Post-Test, with a t-value (8.35) greater than the 1.976 critical t-value and a p-value (6.18E-14) below the 0.05 significance level. Additionally, $\mathbf{8 2. 6 7 \%}$ found the feedback mechanism effective, and $\mathbf{6 2. 6 7 \%}$ expressed interest in a cybersecurity career after playing the game. These findings indicate that the game not only effectively improved the participants’ cybersecurity knowledge and career interests, but also enhanced their learning experience through feedback. Furthermore, ForenSEEK received an overall mean score of 6.29 out of 7, with a low standard deviation of 0.15, reflecting that respondents “Strongly Agree” on the 8 Game User Experience Satisfaction Scale (GUESS) Subscales: Usability/ Playability, Narratives, Player Engrossment, Enjoyment, Creative Freedom, Audio Aesthetics, Personal Gratitude, and Visual Aesthetics. Therefore, ForenSEEK offers a practical approach to bridge the cybersecurity gap by innovating the way cybersecurity is learned.

articleTitle: Optimized Ensemble Learning for Chronic Kidney Disease Prognostication: A Stratified Cross-Validation Approach
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a critical global health issue necessitating early and accurate diagnosis to mitigate its progression. This study presents a comprehensive machine learning framework for CKD prediction, employing advanced ensemble methods optimized through rigorous hyperparameter tuning and validated using 10 -fold Stratified Cross-Validation. The models implemented include Support Vector Machines (SVM), LightGBM, CatBoost, Random Forest, and a Stacking ensemble integrating LightGBM, SVM and Random Forest. The framework addresses challenges in handling categorical data with Label Encoding, imputation of missing values, and feature scaling for models sensitive to data distributions. Experimental results demonstrate that the Stacking ensemble achieves superior performance with an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 5 \%}$, outperforming individual models, with CatBoost and Random Forest also exhibiting strong predictive power. Feature importance analysis further enhances interpretability, aligning with clinical markers relevant to CKD. This work underscores the potential of optimized ensemble learning models to improve diagnostic accuracy and interpretability in clinical decision support systems for CKD.

articleTitle: Quantifying the Benefits of Implementing Big Data Analytics on Consumers’ Online Purchase Intentions in e-Commerce
abstract: The digital revolution has reshaped the global economy, especially e-commerce. Innovative technologies such as big data analytics, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing drive this transformation, enabling companies to make informed business decisions and influence consumers’ online purchasing behaviour. This study explores empirical evidence for the benefits of using big data analytics (BDA) to influence consumers’ online purchasing decisions in e-commerce. Primary data was collected via an online survey targeting 300 customers with online shopping experience on platforms that have adopted the digital technologies of BDA. Statistical methods used in this study included questionnaire design, reliability test, descriptive analysis, and multiple regression modelling and diagnostics. The findings indicate that the benefits of implementing BDA in e-commerce for information search, recommendation systems, consumer services, dynamic pricing, security and fraud detection are strongly associated with consumers’ online purchasing intentions. The study underscores the importance of businesses leveraging BDA, as the benefits significantly and positively impact consumers’ purchasing intentions in e-commerce while addressing security and fraud detection concerns that undermine its advantage. Nevertheless, we encourage all companies to leverage BDA implementation in their digital marketplace, which ultimately contributes to achieving e-commerce goals, such as increased market reach, cost reduction, and revenue growth.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Model of Information Security Compliance and Protection Behavior through Stimulus-Organism-Response Theory
abstract: Healthcare organizations face significant data breach risks due to human error, despite technological advancements. Despite previous research, we still don’t fully understand how individual, organizational, and technical factors affect healthcare security behavior. This study explores the role of individual, organizational, and technical factors in shaping information security compliance and protection behavior in healthcare institutions. Utilizing the Stimulus-Organism-Response model, the research investigates how external pressures, such as information security regulations and policies, alongside internal factors like security training and education, incident experience, and technical controls, influence employee behavior and awareness. Findings reveal that while technical measures are essential, human factors—especially security awareness—are pivotal in preventing breaches. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for compliance and protection behavior based on the stimulus-organism-response model.

articleTitle: A Review of Ginger Disease Detection Technique using Artificial Intelligence (AI)
abstract: Ginger plant disease is a main concern of ginger agriculture industry. While at the same time, traditional methods of detecting ginger plant disease does not seems efficient and effective in terms of resources spent. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques, is attracting growing interest as potential solutions. This study provides an overview of ginger plant diseases, including common examples and their respective symptoms. In addition, the general process of plant disease detection which was applied in ginger disease detection will also be described. Furthermore, reviews of studies on the use of ML and DL models in the detection of ginger disease will be performed. At the end of this study, the challenges associated with ginger disease detection are discussed, highlighting areas for future research.

articleTitle: A Game-Based Learning Application for Engineering Education
abstract: Integrating game-based learning application in engineering education provides a dynamic approach to increase student engagement and understanding. The goal of this initiative is not only to boost interest in engineering programs, but also to develop a more viable and sustainable future for the engineering workforce. This paper presents the design and development of a game-based learning application titled Electroguys, in delivering electrical engineering concepts to high school students. The teaching materials includes interactive games such as “Circuit Rush” and “Energy Expedition” that reinforce learning through problem solving and active participation. The propose work aims to equip students with the skills, knowledge and enthusiasm needed to succeed in the dynamic field of electrical engineering. Testing and feedback show significant improvements in student motivation and retention.

articleTitle: Enhancing Learning Management Systems with Artificial Intelligence in Vocational Education in Malaysia
abstract: The integration of Learning Management Systems (LMS) in vocational colleges has revolutionized educational delivery by streamlining content management and communication. The study aims to identify Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies that improve user engagement, personalize learning experiences, and optimize administrative tasks within LMS platforms. It investigates the utilization of LMS in Malaysian vocational colleges and evaluates how AI technologies can enhance its effectiveness. These advancements lead to higher student satisfaction, improved academic performance, and more efficient administrative operations. The study highlights the critical role of AI in maximizing LMS capabilities, thereby fostering a more effective and personalized learning environment in vocational education. Future research should focus on longitudinal studies to assess the long-term impacts and address implementation challenges, positioning Malaysian vocational colleges at the forefront of educational innovation.

articleTitle: Predicting League of Legends Match Outcomes Through Machine Learning Models Using Past Match Player Performance
abstract: League of Legends (LoL) is a popular multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) game with a significant competitive player base. Despite its skill-based matchmaking system, achieving ideal balance remains challenging due to variations in player performance based on chosen champions and roles. This study analyzes over 11,000 ranked matches, using player metrics like Overall Win Rate, Role Win Rate, and Champion Win Rate to train machine learning models: Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, and Deep Neural Networks. The results show that all three models achieved an average accuracy of $97.5 \%$, with Champion Win Rate emerging as the most important predictor of match outcomes. These findings provide insights into how past player performance influences match outcomes.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Emotion Recognition
abstract: Emotion recognition is crucial in fields like human-computer interaction, mental health, and social robotics, where understanding and responding to emotions is key to effective communication. Recent research has shown that combining multiple types of data, such as visual and audio signals, can improve the accuracy of emotion recognition systems. In this study, we present a multi-modal emotion recognition model that considers both visual and audio features to enhance emotion classification. The model extracts facial features from video frames using OpenFace and EfficientNet, and utilises the Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) and other audio features extracted by Wav2Vec 2 from soundtracks. The model uses a transformer-based feature analyzer to capture temporal dependencies and interactions between the modalities. Finally, the combined feature representation is fed into a classifier that predicts the emotional state. This approach allows for a more comprehensive understanding of emotions by leveraging both visual and auditory cues, leading to improved accuracy in emotion recognition tasks. Experiments show that the proposed model performs better than existing models on the RAVDESS and SAVEE datasets.

articleTitle: Application of Unsupervised Anomaly Detection on Time Series Medical Radiation Data
abstract: This paper examines the application of three unsupervised anomaly detection techniques on time series medical radiation data: Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) autoencoder, Reconstruction Convolutional Autoencoder (RCAE) and Isolation Forest. An unlabelled time series radiotherapy dataset with artificially inserted anomalies was used to evaluate the performance of these models, with a goal to identify anomalous data in medical radiation which could signify dangerous spikes or inadequate dosages for a patient. The results indicates that the LSTM autoencoder model showed the best performance in accurately detecting anomalies within in the medical radiation dataset, due to its ability to capture long-term temporal dependencies. Meanwhile, RCAE performed the best on a separate dataset from the Numenta Anomaly Benchmark (NAB), suggesting its strength in handling datasets with structured or spatial patterns. The study highlights the importance of considering temporal relationships for anomaly detection in sequential data and provides insights into the strengths of different models for specific applications.

articleTitle: Development of an RFID-Based Record Management Web Portal for Goats Towards Precision Livestock Farming
abstract: For sustainable and profitable livestock production, precision livestock farming necessitates the formulation of optimal husbandry and management practices across various aspects, including tracking individual animal pedigrees, monitoring milk production performance, assessing health status, managing feeding and nutrition, making culling decisions, and implementing selective breeding. Data-driven decision-making is essential in these practices, and comprehensive and efficient record keeping is fundamental to producing the reliable data needed for them. This paper presents the design and development of an RFID-based record management system tailored for small to medium-sized goat farms, specifically implemented at the Small Ruminant Center of Central Luzon State University. The system integrates RFID technology to streamline data capturing and management processes, enhancing the efficiency of routine herd operations such as milking, weighing, and health treatments. The system comprises four primary components: animal identification and data capturing, task management, financial management, and real-time reporting and data analysis. Upon deployment, practical enhancements were made based on real-world usage, including improved security measures, streamlined data input processes, and enhanced user notifications. The system was evaluated by IT experts using ISO/IEC 25010 criteria, receiving high ratings across functionality, performance, and compatibility. This system will contribute to the advancement of record management practices for goat farming, leading to increased production and improved livelihoods for small ruminant farmers in the Philippines.

articleTitle: Bringing Culture to Life: A Usability Study of Web-AR Folklore Storytelling
abstract: Learning about culture is essential, and expanding the methods of cultural education beyond traditional learning is crucial. Technology offers new opportunities to not only enhance cultural learning but also promote tourism by introducing cultural elements through innovative platforms. This study evaluates the usability of a web-AR app designed to introduce the Bajau Samah culture through folklore storytelling, providing both an educational tool and a tourism promotion method. The app consists of six pages, allowing users to interact with augmented reality (AR) by scanning markers. Users can zoom and rotate 3D models, listen to audio, and read accompanying narratives. A total of 33 participants took part in the usability study, with more than half of them having no prior experience with AR. The System Usability Scale (SUS) score was 83.5%, indicating good usability. While some usability issues were identified and suggestions for improvement were provided, overall, participants enjoyed using the web-AR app and found it effective in educating them about Bajau Samah culture through AR-folklore storytelling.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of CPU Power Consumption for Detecting DGA Botnet Command and Control Communication
abstract: Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA) Botnets represent a significant threat to network security due to their ability to mask Command and Control (C&C) communications with botmaster. Traditional detection methods like domain blacklists have struggle to keep pace with the dynamic nature of these botnets. This research explores an alternative detection approach by investigating the use of CPU power consumption as an indicator for detecting DGA botnet in Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The power consumption data was collected and analyzed from a testbed comprising infected Raspberry Pi devices with DGA-based botnets. Statistical methods that include Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and post-hoc tests, were used to determine if significant differences in CPU power consumption exist across the botnet phases. The results show that CPU power consumption is significantly higher during both the C&C and attack phases compared to normal operation. Additionally, the attack phase exhibits greater power consumption variance, suggesting unstable resource utilization. These findings highlight the potential of using power consumption data as a key metric for identifying botnet activities in IoT systems.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Classification with Histopathological Images using Otsu’s Method and CNN
abstract: Since lung cancer is one of the leading reasons for cancer-associated fatalities worldwide, early and precise identification is crucial to enhancing patient outcomes. Early identification performs a significant character in the survival rate and treatments of lung cancer patients. This paper examines the efficacy of utilizing Otsu’s image segmentation technique in combination with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to classify lung cancer histopathology pictures. This research analysis is carried out by using the publicly released benchmark lungs tissue histopathological imaging dataset LC25000. The efficacy of Otsu’s segmentation on CNN’s F1-score, precision, recall, and accuracy are among the metrics utilized to compare the suggested method’s productiveness. The findings show that using Otsu’s approach greatly improves the model’s productiveness; with segmentation, the architecture achieves an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 1 \%}$. This demonstrates that the CNN with Otsu’s gives a better approach for classifying or detecting lung cancer.

articleTitle: Assessing Data Quality Maturity Models: Enhancing Organizational Readiness and Improvement
abstract: Data quality is crucial in supporting accurate decision-making in today’s digital era. Key attributes such as data completeness, accuracy, consistency, and relevance must be maintained to ensure organizations across various sectors, including finance, healthcare, and education, can optimally utilize data. However, data quality issues such as incompleteness, inaccuracy, and inconsistency often pose significant challenges to accurate decision-making. Invalid or irrelevant data can lead to decision-making errors, ultimately harming business performance and strategy. If data quality is not maintained, decisions based on such data risk being inaccurate and ineffective. In this study, a data quality capability model is proposed and evaluated by six experts, with an average score of 3.7 and a Content Validity Ratio (CVR) of 1, indicating that the model is valid and relevant for implementation. The Fleiss’ Kappa value of 0.481 indicates good agreement among the experts, further supporting the model’s relevance for use within organizations. Implementing this model is expected to help organizations manage their data more effectively and efficiently, resulting in high-quality data that supports accurate decision-making. The application of this model is also expected to enhance organizational performance and competitiveness in the face of increasingly complex data management challenges. This model can be a foundation for achieving higher data quality standards, allowing organizations to strategically leverage data in innovation development and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimizing Data Routing in Wireless Sensor Networks: A Hybrid Approach Using Machine Learning and Tabu Search Mechanisms
abstract: This work presents a new technique for routing data in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), where the extensive sensor nodes are capable of wireless communication, computing, and sensing, mainly for environmental data collection purposes. In WSN setup, the nodes, that transmit data to a central base station, face a vital challenges in data transmission, routing, and congestion management. Various prior protocols have been suggested for these tasks; however, they still have some limitations related to throughput, energy efficiency and network lifetime. Consequently, this paper focuses on optimizing energy use, improving network longevity, and enhancing Quality of Service (QoS) metrics such as active node count and data throughput. To this end, we integrate a machine learning (ML) mechanism with a traditional routing technique, where ML is employed to dynamically adjust routing decisions for better data transmission and congestion management, meanwhile, the Tabu Search algorithm identifies congested routes. Noting that a congestion alert is triggered when the traffic load on a route hits 70 percent, so, this activates our proposed approach to find alternative pathways to the Cluster Head (CH).

articleTitle: On the Estimation of Financial Risk: A Theoretical Exploration Using ARIMA-GARCH Models
abstract: This study investigates the application of advanced statistical models to analyze the Malaysian stock market, with a focus on the ARIMA-GARCH model. Traditional ARIMA models, following the Box-Jenkins approach, are designed to forecast the mean behavior of financial time series, assuming stationarity with constant or seasonally dependent variances. However, these models overlook variations in conditional variance, which are crucial for capturing the nonlinear dynamics often present in financial data. Although the statistical properties of the Malaysian financial market have been widely studied, the adoption of heteroskedastic models that account for non-constant variances remains limited. To address this gap, this research integrates GARCH with ARIMA models to capture both serial dependence and time-varying volatility in daily closing prices. The study focuses on the financial risks of three major Malaysian banks that are Maybank, Public Bank, and CIMB Bank, using a model that effectively reflects market fluctuations. Analyzing daily stock prices from 2000 to 2023, the study employs two key risk measures, namely Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES), which help estimate potential losses under adverse conditions. The findings reveal varying risk levels, with Maybank showing a $\mathbf{1 . 1 \%}$ VaR, CIMB Bank $\mathbf{1 . 7 \%}$, and Public Bank $0.7 \%$. This research offers valuable insights for enhancing risk management practices within Malaysia’s banking sector and provides a framework that can benefit other emerging markets.

articleTitle: ML-Driven Solutions for Chronic Liver Disease: Predictive Models and Prevention Strategies
abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is a major global health issue, often progressing silently until it reaches advanced stages, leading to severe illness and death if not detected early. The liver plays a critical role in filtering toxins and aiding digestion, so any disruption can have serious consequences. Raising awareness about liver health is crucial because early detection can change the disease’s course, opening doors to treatment and even reversing damage in some cases. In the United States, CLD has become a growing health crisis, with increasing deaths linked to conditions like hepatitis $\mathbf{C}$, alcohol-related liver disease, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), largely due to rising obesity rates. These statistics highlight the urgent need for improved prevention, early diagnosis, and treatment strategies. Advances in machine learning (ML) offer new hope in fighting liver disease. Predictive models like RandomForest, LightGBM, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, Ensemble Learning Stacking, and ExtraTrees can accurately forecast the onset and progression of liver disease. These models enable earlier identification of at-risk individuals and more effective interventions, potentially transforming how we manage CLD. By leveraging these technological innovations, we can significantly reduce mortality rates and empower healthcare providers to take swift, decisive action in preventing and treating liver diseases.

articleTitle: Allocate IT: Optimization of Resource Allocation of IT Consultancies Using a Decision Support System
abstract: In the IT industry, efficient resource allocation is crucial, yet many smaller consultancies still rely on outdated manual systems, leading to missed deadlines and overstretched teams. In response, Allocate IT, a web-based platform, was developed to streamline staff assignments based on skills and availability, improving efficiency. Utilizing a decision support system and frequency counting algorithm, it allows project managers to quickly match the right people to the right tasks. The system underwent evaluation using software quality standards, achieving a user satisfaction score of 4.00 out of 5. High ratings were received in Functional Suitability with scores of 4.06 for Completeness and 4.2 for Correctness, in Reliability with Consistency at 4.1 and Availability at 4.2, and in Usability, with a notable 4.5 for User Interface Aesthetics. A confusion matrix analysis showed strong performance in classifying Task 1 (55 correct predictions), though moderate accuracy was noted for Tasks 2 (32 correct) and 7 (39 correct), with some misclassifications between similar tasks. The classification report reflected an overall accuracy of 0.76, with high precision for Tasks 3 (0.88) and 9 (0.85), while Tasks 2 and 8 had lower F1-scores (0.72). Despite these challenges, Allocate IT represents a significant advancement in resource management for IT consultancies, enhancing both efficiency and task allocation accuracy.
